goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the V1 vs V2 feature-flag guard on the cleanup event listener.

goldens.comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same owner mismatch (getId vs getClientId), which causes per-client permissions to be ignored.

goldens.comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out that findByType misses per-client resources because they have no type, which is the core of G3.

goldens.comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions a possible null from getResourceTypeResource leading to an NPE.

goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the unused getEvaluationContext method.

candidates: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) looks up client resources using resourceServer.getId() as the owner filter, but client resources are created with resourceServer.getClientId() as the owner, so per-client permissions are silently ignored and only global 'all clients' permissions take effect

getClientsWithPermission iterates resources by type 'Clients', but client-instance resources created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are stored with no explicit type (defaults to null), causing the method to miss all per-client resources and return an incomplete set

canManage(ClientModel client) only checks the legacy MANAGE_CLIENTS role or a resource-specific permission for that client, but does not check the realm-wide fine-grained manage permission on the Clients resource type, causing admins with only the global V2 manage permission to be incorrectly denied

canView() returns false for admins who have only the all-clients manage permission, breaking realm-wide client visibility since the manage scope should subsume view but the implementation only checks canViewClientDefault() and the view scope

When getOrCreateResource creates a client resource, it sets name to client.getId() but never calls setDisplayName, and getResourceName only special-cases Users, causing client permission listings to show null instead of a human-readable name

hasGrantedPermission() only evaluates the passed resource, so getClientsWithPermission() misses permissions granted through the shared 'all clients' resource, returning an empty set even when canView(client)/canManage(client) would succeed for those clients
